etymologies.etymologyHTML: Clipping of Coca-Cola. See coke (“cola”).

definitions.definition: (countable, uncountable, informal) Cola-based soft drink; (in particular) Coca-Cola.
(countable, informal) A bottle, glass or can of Coca-Cola or a cola-based soft drink.

quote.citation: 1951, J. D. Salinger, The Catcher in the Rye, Boston, Mass.: Little, Brown and Company, →OCLC, page 168:
quote.text: The waiter came up, and I ordered a Coke for her—she didn't drink—and a Scotch and soda for myself, but the sonuvabitch wouldn't bring me one, so I had a Coke, too.

quote.citation: 1958, Franklin Martin, “The Trouble with Mrs. Benton”, in Venus, volume 1, number 1, Garden of Eve Publications, page 16:
quote.text: 'You have a coke and I'll have a beer and we can talk business.'

definitions.definition: (US, especially Southern US, informal) Any soft drink, regardless of type.
